pre_registrations.statement: Restated per review: the near-trivial half is that the two-tier {none, code_only} cascade reaches the three-arm union (109/148 on HumanEval). The non-trivial claim is that union(none, code_only) == union(none, code_only, error) -- T3 is provably dead weight -- and that the two-tier order attains that ceiling at strictly lower repairer-model cost than every order that tries T3.
pre_registrations.falsifier: T3 solves >= 1 coordinate neither T1 nor T2 solves, OR some order containing T3 reaches the ceiling at repairer cost <= the two-tier order's cost.

pre_registrations.statement: Escalating exactly on the n coordinates the verifier marks T1-failing beats escalating on a budget-matched RANDOM selection of n coordinates from the full cohort, by >= 2x on net added passes.

The verifier-targeted escalation also beats a PREDICTED-failure escalation of the same size n, chosen by p_pass_oof (lowest first) and separately by initial_chars (longest first) -- a pipeline with no verifier has to guess, and p_pass_oof is this project's best guess.
pre_registrations.falsifier: either predictor's added passes is within 10% of the verifier's

pre_registrations.statement: At the margin, switching to the next tier's first candidate beats deepening the cheap tier's own candidate list, for some k <= 3.
pre_registrations.falsifier: deepening dominates switching at every testable k <= 3

pre_registrations.statement: Cascade gain tracks Week 9's complementarity: MBPP shows ~0 gain from adding context tiers, since it has only one context-only coordinate.
pre_registrations.falsifier: the T1->T2 cascade adds >= 3 net passes on MBPP
